title: CHAPTER TWELVE. Old Testament sacraments: circumcision and Passover
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): II. There stand as chiefly two: CIRCUMCISION and ye PASSOVER. Other signs we do not here count under ye stricter notion belonging toward sacraments. — Old Testament sacraments stand as those handed down and instituted by God for ye Jewish people which through an earthly thing designated ye coming Messiah for conferring and sealing Gospel grace. — CHAPTER TWELVE. On ye sacraments belonging toward ye Old Testament.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER TWELVE. On the sacraments of the Old Testament.
Old Testament sacraments are those handed down and instituted by God for the Jewish people which through an earthly thing designated the coming Messiah for conferring and sealing Gospel grace.
II. There are chiefly two: CIRCUMCISION and the PASSOVER. Other signs we do not here count under the stricter notion of sacraments.
source_text: CAPUT DUODECIMUM, De sacramentis veteris testamenti. Sacramenta V.T. sunt, quae populo Judaico a Deo tradita & instituta per rem terrenam Messiam venturum designabant ad conferendam et obsignandam Euangelii gratiam. II. Sunt autem potissimum duo, CIRCUMCISIO & PASCHA. Alia enim signa sub arctiore sacramentorum notione hic non censemus.
